correctness.rationale: A Γ-invariant nonempty simplex of all inter-SCC arcs gives an explicit equivariant cone. In a strongly connected component, the natural sink-set map to the opposite proper Boolean lattice has fibers equivariantly contractible under stabilizers: adding all arcs entering a prescribed nonempty proper S cannot create a directed cycle because no arc can leave S. Thévenaz–Webb Theorem 1 establishes the Γ-equivalence. Natural join of components, including component-permuting automorphisms and zero/singleton cases, identifies the canonical representation sphere. Fixed dimension is vertex-orbit count minus SCC-orbit count and the determinant character follows from an orthogonal permutation-module splitting. Standalone finite checks reproduce 2811 instances but are not used as proof.
